results.summary_before: This factory test module is designed to verify all I/O pins of an ASIC and has three modes: mirroring input pins to outputs, mirroring bidirectional pins to outputs, and outputting an 8-bit counter on both output and bidirectional pins. Mode selection is controlled by rst_n and sel signals, with the counter incrementing every clock cycle and resetting when rst_n is low. The design is written in Verilog and occupies a single tile. It is intended for manufacturing test and requires no external hardware beyond the ASIC itself.
results.summary: This project is a minimal SHA-256 hash core implemented in Verilog with a single-cycle-round architecture. It occupies a 2x2 tile area and uses an addressed register bus with 6-bit register addressing, a read/write select, an IO clock, and 8-bit data lines. The documentation is incomplete, with TODO placeholders for how-it-works and testing instructions. No external hardware is needed beyond a method of interacting with the bus to transfer commands and data.
